## Sanity check on the extra $800 to channel B

**Your instinct that B is performing well is right, but "another $800" won't get you what you're picturing, because of a capacity wall, not a marketing one.**

**Channel B, most recent complete quarter (Q2 2026, Apr 1–Jun 30), from `jobs`/`crm_leads`/`ledger` and the `net_contribution` metric:**
- Spend: $800
- Leads: 40, won: 18 (45% win rate)
- Revenue $27,000, job margin $10,800, net contribution (margin less spend) $10,000 → roughly 12.5x return on the $800, vs channel A's ~7x ($1,000 spend → $7,000 net contribution) in the same quarter. So yes, B is the better channel right now.

**But the growth trend is not a spend story.** Ledger spend on channel B has been flat at exactly $800 every quarter for at least five quarters running (Q3-2025 through Q2-2026, `ledger` kind=channel_spend). Over that same flat-spend period, net contribution climbed steadily: $4,428.68 → $5,040.82 → $6,412.16 → $10,000.00. Since the input (spend) never moved, we have zero historical evidence of how leads or jobs respond to a change in spend. Any projection of what an extra $800 buys would be a guess dressed up as a number, and I won't give you one.

**The bigger issue: channel B is 100% backflow work (64 of 64 jobs, `jobs.service_line`), and per policy only certified techs can be scheduled to it.** Checking `certifications`: only two techs were ever backflow-certified, T5 and T3. T5 left the company 2026-02-28. That leaves T3 alone. In Q2 2026, T3 was already scheduled 488.8 of his 520 available hours, 94% utilization, only about 31 hours of slack left in the whole quarter. Average backflow job is 6 hours, so that's roughly 5 more jobs of headroom, not the dozens more leads a spend increase might generate.

**So the sanity check: spending $1,600 instead of $800 on channel B this quarter would likely buy more leads you can't service**, since there is effectively one technician who can legally take backflow jobs and he is nearly full. That's lost/wasted spend risk, not upside, until capacity is fixed.

**What I'd do instead:** get a second tech backflow-certified (or bring T5 back / verify an existing cert covers it) before adding spend. Once there's real slack, run the $1,600 as a genuine test quarter and compare leads/CPL/win-rate against the $800 baseline, that's the only way to actually learn B's spend elasticity, which today's data cannot tell you.

ANSWER: Channel B is your best-performing channel (about 12.5x net contribution on Q2 2026 spend versus ~7x for channel A), but its spend has never varied so there's no data to say what another $800 would buy, and the real constraint is that all of B's work is backflow service, which only one technician (T3) is certified for and he was already at 94% utilization in Q2. Doubling B's spend now risks buying leads that can't be serviced rather than more revenue; fix backflow tech capacity first, then test the spend increase with a real before/after comparison.
